gist: JJ Gabriel featured in Manchester United's team photo despite his desire to leave.
The teenager decided to seek a departure after missing a Champions League match.
Manchester United still hold his registration amid interest from top European clubs.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: JJ Gabriel was included in Manchester United's official senior team photograph, taken on 8 September. Two days later, he played his final match for the club and announced his intention to leave. His decision followed his omission from Michael Carrick's squad for a Champions League fixture against Sabah FK.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Gabriel is now pursued by leading European sides, including Real Madrid and Barcelona. Manchester United maintain they demonstrated commitment to the forward by providing first-team care, regular access to senior staff, and lobbying the Premier League regarding his shirt name.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: United still hold Gabriel's registration and have attempted to reconcile with him. The club would consider legal action if evidence of illegal inducement by another club or agent emerges.

gist: Fifa switched to a longer international break to aid player welfare and travel.
A number of players have returned from international duty carrying injuries.
Managers and unions have raised concerns over high player workloads and travel strains.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Fifa replaced five two-week international breaks with four breaks, including a new three-week gap in late September and early October. Numerous players picked up injuries while representing their countries, including Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappe and Alex Scott, while others withdrew before matches.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The changes were made with player welfare and reduced cross-continent travel in mind ahead of the 2026 World Cup. However, clubs face mounting injury concerns, leading players' unions and managers to question whether the increased demands and training styles are harming players.

Medvedev hit a spectator in the face with a ball in annoyance.
The player lost his points and prize money from the tournament.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Daniil Medvedev faced Novak Djokovic in a semi-final match. While trailing in the second set, Medvedev struck a ball in anger that hit a front-row spectator in the face. Following discussions with officials, the umpire disqualified Medvedev from the match.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Defaults in professional tennis are uncommon and typically happen due to code of conduct breaches. Medvedev received an immediate disqualification for the serious offence, resulting in the loss of his accumulated tournament points and prize money.

NFL.title: 'Money-grab' or celebration? NFL kicks off London series
NFL.standfirst: The NFL kicked off this season's series of London games on Sunday but the build-up was overshadowed by anger from long-term fans over ticket prices.

articles.title: 'Money-grab' or celebration? NFL kicks off London series
articles.standfirst: The NFL kicked off this season's series of London games on Sunday but the build-up was overshadowed by anger from long-term fans over ticket prices.

gist: Thousands of tickets remained available for some NFL London games due to slow sales.
Fans criticised steep price hikes and the scrapping of discounted season-ticket packages.
Despite complaints, the games continue to attract large crowds and celebrity attendees.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The NFL kicked off its London series with a game between the Washington Commanders and Indianapolis Colts. Although one upcoming fixture sold out quickly, thousands of tickets were initially left unsold, prompting the NFL to drop prices and offer discounted or free tickets.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Long-term supporters felt priced out by ticket increases that exceeded inflation and the removal of season-ticket packages. Some fans viewed the changes as a money-grab that alienated loyal attendees in favour of newer consumers.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The NFL continues its international series with upcoming matches in London, featuring teams such as the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars.

quotes.text: I find the prices now mind-boggling
It felt like a kick to the head for a lot of loyal fans

sections.heading: What happened

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Gabriel is a target for several top European clubs, including Real Madrid and Barcelona. Manchester United hold his registration and would consider legal action if illegal inducement emerges.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Gabriel is set to turn 16 and his next involvement in a United game will virtually certainly be as an opposition player.
